claims.claim: hitTier still occupies a small, closed discrete range {0,1,2,3} at full roster scale: pooled non-terminator distribution is {0:31, 1:789, 2:529, 3:512} across n=1861 entries (min=0, max=3, distinct_count=4) -- identical range to round 1's 4-character sample, now backed by 20x more data. Terminator-only rows are NOT uniformly hitTier=0 either: {0:118, 1:25, 2:22, 3:21} across n=186 terminator rows -- only 118/186 (63.44%) terminator rows carry hitTier=0. jpower's damage fields remain far wider/more granular (totalDamage: 13 distinct values across 0-600; damage1: 16 distinct values across 0-400), unchanged from round 1 since jpower.json was not re-exported by P1. The round-1 shape-comparison (small closed enum vs. wide damage range) SURVIVES at full scale.

open_questions: Why do 68/186 (36.6%) terminator rows carry a nonzero hitTier instead of the expected 0 sentinel -- are these genuinely mid-list markers rather than true end-of-list terminators (see the isTerminator-variance claim below), or does the exporter's terminator-detection heuristic misclassify some non-terminal rows?

claims.claim: collisionType=5 -> hitTier=3 does NOT hold up as a 'strong categorical predictor' at full roster scale -- the round-1 UNSURE cap on this claim is now decisively justified. Pooled fraction drops from round 1's 14/16=87.50% (n=4 chars) to 216/454=47.58% (n=61 chars) at full scale, essentially a coin-flip. Per-character breakdown of the 61/74 characters with any collisionType=5 entries: only 18 are at 100% tier-3, 7 are at 0% tier-3, and the remaining 36 (59.0% of chars-with-ct5) are 'partial' -- neither extreme. Example spread: dg_b_02 is 13/13=100%, while op_b_03 is 1/33=3.03% and bb_b_04 is 0/4=0%.

Per-character block 'PER-CHARACTER collisionType=5 -> hitTier=3 rule check (battle, n=74 chars)': 'characters with >=1 collisionType=5 entry: 61 / 74'; per-char lines include 'dg_b_02: 13/13 = 1.0000', 'op_b_03: 1/33 = 0.0303', 'bb_b_04: 0/4 = 0.0000'; summary line '-> chars at 100% tier3: 18; chars at 0% tier3: 7; partial (neither 0% nor 100%): 36; total chars-with-ct5: 61'.
open_questions: Is collisionType=5's tier-3 association concentrated in a specific move-category subset (e.g. supers/finishers for some characters but not others), such that a per-character-archetype split (not attempted here) would reveal a real but narrower rule -- or is collisionType=5 simply a generic 'ranged/special' bucket with hitTier assigned independently per move by the designer?

claims.claim: collisionType=3 -> hitTier=1 is similarly weaker at full scale than round 1 suggested, though it retains a modest majority tendency. Pooled fraction: 522/885=58.98% (round 1: 28/43=65.12%). All 74/74 characters have >=1 collisionType=3 entry (making this the most universal collisionType), but hitTier=1 is a strict majority of a character's own collisionType=3 entries in only 43/74 (58.1%) of characters -- e.g. db_b_01 (the round-1 char that flipped the pattern) is still non-majority at 5/12=41.67% tier-1 in the full data, corroborating round 1's data-consistency verdict that this character was a genuine counter-example, not noise.
claims.evidence_data: Section 2: 'collisionType=3 (n=885): {0: 2, 1: 522, 2: 280, 3: 81}' -> '-> POOLED collisionType=3 tier-1 fraction: 522/885 = 0.5898'. Per-character block: 'characters with >=1 collisionType=3 entry: 74 / 74'; 'db_b_01: 5/12 = 0.4167'; summary '-> chars where hitTier=1 is a STRICT MAJORITY of their collisionType=3 entries: 43 / 74'.
open_questions: Given collisionType=3 appears in all 74 characters (unlike collisionType=5's 61/74), is collisionType=3 a baseline/default hitbox category rather than a move-strength indicator, which would explain why its hitTier association is weaker and less consistent than a true tier-selector field would produce?

claims.claim: knockback does NOT scale monotonically with hitTier, and this conclusion is now robust at full scale rather than an artifact of one outlier character (round 1's critic REFUTED the 4-character version of this claim because a single file, bl_b_01, drove the whole pooled pattern). At n=1861, pooled avg-knockback-by-tier is [7.65, 14.76, 15.85, 12.42] for tiers [0,1,2,3] -- rising then dropping at tier 3, confirmed non-monotonic. Critically, this is now a population-level, not single-file, pattern: of 74 characters with knockback data across >=2 hitTiers, only 17 (23.0%) show a monotonic non-decreasing avg-knockback-by-tier trend; 55 (74.3%) are non-monotonic; 2 have insufficient tier diversity to test. A large majority of INDIVIDUAL characters, not just the pooled average, fail to show hitTier-as-knockback-ranking.

Per-character: 'monotonic non-decreasing avg-knockback-by-tier: 17 / 74'; 'non-monotonic: 55 / 74'; 'insufficient data (<2 distinct hitTier values present): 2 / 74'.
open_questions: With 74.3% of characters individually non-monotonic and the pooled sequence dipping specifically at tier 3 (not tier 1 as round 1's small sample suggested), is tier 3 a qualitatively different category (e.g. 'special/unblockable' rather than 'highest knockback') rather than simply the top of a knockback-ranked scale?

claims.claim: The round-1 hypothesis that projectileId=-32 is a single fixed sentinel value is REFUTED at full roster scale. Across 2047 battle entries, 47 (2.30%) have nonzero projectileId spanning 15 distinct values: -34, -32, -31, -30, -28, -26, -25, -24, -23, -22, -20, -19, -18, 18, 36 -- predominantly negative in a -18..-34 band, but not exclusively (18 and 36 are positive, seen on oj_b_01 and yh_b_03 respectively). 25/74 characters (33.8%) have at least one nonzero-projectileId entry. Support files show an even richer picture: 172/747 (23.03%) entries nonzero (10x the battle rate) across 25 distinct nonzero values (adds -33, 3, 6, 7, 9, 10, 16, 17 to the value set seen in battle files). This is far more consistent with projectileId being a real per-projectile-type identifier/enum than a single boolean-like sentinel.

Section 7 (SUPPORT): 'SUPPORT nonzero-projectileId entries: 172 / 747 = 0.2303'; 'SUPPORT distinct nonzero projectileId values: [-34, -33, -32, -31, -30, -29, -28, -27, -26, -25, -24, -23, -22, -21, -20, -19, -18, 3, 6, 7, 9, 10, 16, 17, 18] (count=25)'.
open_questions: Do the negative values (-18..-34, a contiguous-looking band) index into one projectile-definition table while the rare positive values (18, 36 in battle; 3,6,7,9,10,16,17,18 in support) index a different or overlapping table -- and does either band's numeric ordering correlate with a known projectile roster order documented elsewhere (e.g. docs/research/Character-Mapping.md)?

claims.claim: collisionType=4 is NOT a necessary condition for nonzero projectileId at full scale, refuting round 1's 'necessary but not sufficient' framing. Of all 47 nonzero-projectileId entries (including terminator rows), 35 (74.47%) have collisionType=4, 11 (23.40%) have collisionType=5, and 1 (2.13%) has collisionType=1 -- the union of collisionType in {4,5} covers 46/47 (97.87%), so the real pattern is 'collisionType 4 OR 5', not '4 only'. A further structural nuance: 8/47 (17.02%) nonzero-projectileId entries are themselves isTerminator=True rows (e.g. nk_b_01, oj_b_01, rk_b_01, yh_b_03, na_b_02 x3, hs_b_01) -- terminator rows are not always pure zero/sentinel rows; some carry real projectileId payloads.
claims.evidence_data: Section 3: 'collisionType==4 entries (non-terminator, battle): 272; of those with projectileId!=0: 31'; 'nonzero-projectileId entries with collisionType != 4: 12' (11 of these are collisionType=5, one is collisionType=1: 'hs_b_01', 1, 0, -19); 'collisionType distribution across ALL 47 nonzero-projectileId entries (incl. terminator rows): {1: 1, 4: 35, 5: 11}' with lines 'collisionType=1: 1/47 = 0.0213', 'collisionType=4: 35/47 = 0.7447', 'collisionType=5: 11/47 = 0.2340', 'collisionType in {4,5} union: 46/47 = 0.9787'; 'nonzero-projectileId entries that are ALSO isTerminator=True rows: 8/47 = 0.1702' with the 8 rows printed.
open_questions: Does collisionType=5 with nonzero projectileId represent a structurally different projectile mechanic than collisionType=4 (e.g. a homing/tracking vs. straight-line distinction), and why would a terminator-flagged row (isTerminator=True) ever need a live projectileId payload -- is isTerminator possibly a different bit than 'last entry in list' (e.g. 'end of this move's hitbox sub-list' within a multi-move file)?

claims.claim: hitProperties per-character constancy holds for a majority but is NOT 'near-perfectly file-constant' as round 1's 4-character sample suggested. At full scale, 48/74 characters (64.86%) have a single hitProperties value across their entire file, but 26/74 (35.14%) show 2 or 3 distinct values within their own file (e.g. bb_b_01/02/03 all mix {1,3}; db_b_04 mixes {0,1,5}; nn_b_01 and op_b_05 and yo_b_01 each mix {0,1,2}). A previously unseen 3rd bit also appears: hitProperties=5 (0b101, bit2 set) occurs once in db_b_04, and bit1 now occurs WITHOUT bit0 in 23/2047 entries (value=2, 0b10) -- both contradict round 1's 'only two bits, bit1 never alone' observation. Support files show a similar but somewhat stronger constancy majority: 168/206 (81.55%) constant-within-file vs 38/206 (18.45%) varying, and support hitProperties includes value 6 (0b110, bits 1+2) not seen in battle files.
claims.evidence_data: Section 4: 'characters with a SINGLE hitProperties value across their whole file: 48 / 74 = 0.6486'; 'characters with >1 distinct hitProperties value in their own file (VARYING): 26 / 74 = 0.3514' with all 26 chars and their value sets printed (bb_b_01/02/03: [1,3]; db_b_04: [0,1,5]; nn_b_01/op_b_05/yo_b_01: [0,1,2]); 'POOLED hitProperties (battle, n=2047): {0: 1051, 1: 599, 2: 23, 3: 373, 5: 1}'; 'distinct hitProperties values observed (battle): [0, 1, 2, 3, 5]'; 'bit1 (0x2) set count: 396/2047 ... bit1-set-without-bit0 count: 23'. Section 7: 'POOLED hitProperties (SUPPORT, n=747): {0: 299, 1: 15, 2: 205, 3: 213, 6: 15}'; 'SUPPORT per-file hitProperties constancy: constant-within-file=168/206 = 0.8155; varying=38/206 = 0.1845'.
open_questions: Is hitProperties a per-move-family trait that a character 'unlocks' additional bits for on stronger/alt moves (explaining within-file variation as authored, not noise), and does the newly observed bit2 (0x4) correspond to a documented hit property (e.g. armor-break, guard-crush) in any external JUS moveset reference?

claims.claim: The round-1 observation that the two nonzero-projectileId entries had 'opposite' hitProperties values (3 vs 0) does not generalize and was almost certainly n=2 noise -- at full scale (n=47 nonzero-projectileId entries) the distribution is {0: 14, 1: 32, 3: 1}, dominated by hitProperties=1 (68.09%), not split evenly. This is a real, replacing finding: hitProperties=1's baseline rate across ALL battle entries is only 599/2047=29.26%, but WITHIN the nonzero-projectileId subset it jumps to 32/47=68.09% -- more than double the baseline rate, suggesting hitProperties bit0 (0x1) alone (without bit1) is enriched among projectile-flagged hitboxes specifically.
claims.evidence_data: Section 4: 'hitProperties distribution on the 47 nonzero-projectileId entries (battle, full scale): {0: 14, 1: 32, 3: 1}'; 'hitProperties==1 baseline rate (all battle entries): 599/2047 = 0.2926'; 'hitProperties==1 rate WITHIN nonzero-projectileId subset: 32/47 = 0.6809'.
open_questions: Does hitProperties bit0 (0x1) alone specifically mark 'this hitbox belongs to a projectile-class attack' (as opposed to bit1 marking something orthogonal, like a block-type), which would explain both the 68% enrichment here and the bit1-without-bit0 cases (value=2) seen exclusively on non-projectile entries?

claims.claim: damageFlags==0 is common but is NOT a clean majority at full roster scale, softening round 1's 'majority case' framing (52/91=57.14% in the 4-char sample). Pooled full-scale fraction: 872/1861=46.86% (battle, non-terminator) -- essentially a coin-flip, slightly under half. Per-character variance is extreme: bu_b_01 and sk_b_01 have damageFlags==0 on 0/31 and 0/14 entries respectively (0.00%, i.e. NEVER zero), while dt_b_04 (a 1-entry file) is 1/1=100%; only 1/74 characters is at 100% zero and only 2/74 are at 0% zero, with the bulk of characters spread across the full 0-100% range. Support files show a nearly identical pooled rate: 211/486=43.42%.

claims.claim: hitModifier is NOT constant at 0 at full roster scale -- this directly supersedes and breaks round 1's CONFIRMED_STATIC claim ('hitModifier is constant at 0 across all 92 collision entries'). Across the full 2047-entry battle corpus, 9 entries (0.44%) have a nonzero hitModifier, spanning values {2, 6, 18, 20, 25, 34} across 6 distinct characters: bl_b_03 (18), db_b_07 (34, on a terminator row), op_b_03 (20 and 25, two separate entries), sk_b_02 (6, twice), and tr_b_01 (2, three times). This is corroborated cross-population: item_collision.json independently has hitModifier=30 on one entry, and support files independently show hitModifier in {10, 15, 20} -- three separate populations (battle, support, item) all show hitModifier taking real nonzero values, confirming it is a live field, just rare in the battle-file population specifically.

open_questions: What game mechanic does hitModifier=2/6/18/20/25/34/30 encode given it is rare and character-specific (bl_b_03, db_b_07, op_b_03, sk_b_02, tr_b_01, plus item and several supports) -- is it a per-move damage/knockback scaling multiplier reserved for a small subset of 'special-cased' attacks across the roster?

claims.claim: isTerminator does NOT follow a simple 'exactly one terminator row per file' convention -- round 1's 4-file sample (3 files with 0 terminators, 1 file with exactly 1) massively understated the real variance. At full scale, the terminator-count-per-file histogram is {0:27, 1:13, 2:6, 3:9, 4:8, 5:3, 6:2, 7:2, 8:2, 9:1, 36:1} -- 27/74 characters (36.5%) have ZERO terminator rows at all, while kn_b_01 (60 entries) has 36 terminator rows, more than half its own file. This strongly suggests isTerminator marks the end of per-MOVE hitbox sub-lists within a character's file (multiple moves, multiple terminators) rather than a single end-of-file sentinel, consistent with kn_b_01 (many small moves) having many terminators and single/small-movelist characters having none. The round-1 'sentinel-looking values' description of the one observed terminator row (damageFlags=255, knockback=255) is only a MAJORITY pattern at scale, not universal: 116/186 (62.37%) terminator rows have both damageFlags==255 AND knockback==255; 145/186 (77.96%) have damageFlags==255 alone; 157/186 (84.41%) have knockback==255 alone.

open_questions: If isTerminator delimits per-move hitbox sub-lists rather than end-of-file, is there a companion field (subType, or an index derivable from frameStart resets) that marks the START of each sub-list, which would let a future pass segment each character's ~28-entry-average file into individual move hitbox groups -- this would also supply the missing collision<->jpower join key both rounds have flagged as absent?

claims.claim: Support files (*_s_*, n=206, secondary scope) diverge from battle files on every axis re-tested, generally showing MORE variance and a higher projectile-related signal: (1) collisionType=5->hitTier=3 fraction is 77/206=37.38% in supports vs 216/454=47.58% in battle -- the rule is weaker still for supports; collisionType=3->hitTier=1 is stronger for supports at 39/52=75.00% vs battle's 522/885=58.98%, but on a much smaller n. (2) projectileId nonzero rate is 172/747=23.03% in supports, roughly 10x the battle rate of 47/2047=2.30% -- consistent with support characters (pets/helpers/thrown items) being disproportionately projectile-like entities themselves. (3) hitProperties per-file constancy is somewhat MORE consistent for supports (168/206=81.55% constant) than battle (48/74=64.86% constant). (4) damageFlags==0 rate is nearly identical between the two populations: 211/486=43.42% (support) vs 872/1861=46.86% (battle).

open_questions: Does the ~10x higher projectileId-nonzero rate in support files reflect that support entities (assist characters, thrown helpers) are mechanically implemented AS projectiles at the engine level (i.e. support collision structs and true projectile structs share the same schema and field semantics), which would mean 'projectileId' is better understood as a general 'spawned-sub-entity id' rather than something specific to ranged attacks?

claims.claim: Core structural/schema facts from round 1 remain exactly true at full scale (281 files, not 4): the collision entry schema (23 fields) and jpower entry schema (20 fields) still share ZERO field names; every one of the 281 collision files (74 battle + 206 support + 1 item) uses the identical 23-key entry schema (1 distinct key-set observed); reserved0-3 are still uniformly (0,0,0,0) across all 2047 battle entries; the damageFlagsLow/hasSpecialFlag bitfield decomposition (damageFlagsLow==damageFlags&0x3F, hasSpecialFlag==bool(damageFlags&0x40)) still has zero mismatches across all 2047 battle entries; and the exporter's 'count' field matches len(entries) with zero mismatches across battle (74), support (206), and item (1) files. Structural ranges DID widen substantially at scale though: durationMult now spans 12 distinct values {0,1,2,5,10,16,25,30,40,50,100,120} (was {0,10,100} in round 1) with 30/1861 (1.61%) nonzero entries; width/height ranges widened to [-35,47] and [-33,30] respectively, with negative width/height now at 192/1861=10.32% of entries; extFlags is nonzero on 107/2047=5.23% of entries (was 0% observed as a formal claim in round 1, though nonzero rows were printed).

open_questions: Now that durationMult, width/height, and extFlags all show meaningfully more variance at full scale than round 1's 4-character sample suggested, would a dedicated durationMult/extFlags-focused mining pass (not attempted this round beyond raw distributions) reveal a correlation with move category or hitbox shape that a 4-character sample could never have surfaced?

suggested_next_angles: The isTerminator-variance finding (0 to 36 terminator rows per file, correlated with total entry count) strongly suggests collision files are internally segmented into per-move hitbox sub-lists rather than being one flat list per character; a follow-up pass should attempt to segment each of the 74 files on isTerminator boundaries and check whether segment COUNT per character correlates with that character's jpower entry count (avg 4.20/char) -- if segment count ~= jpower-block size for several characters, that is the collision<->jpower join key both round 1 and round 2 have been unable to find via field-name matching alone.

projectileId's newly-discovered 15 (battle) / 25 (support) distinct nonzero values, mostly clustered in a -18..-34 band, are a strong candidate for a small lookup/enum table; cross-referencing these exact integer values against any already-decoded projectile-definition table or entity-type enum elsewhere in the ROM (disassembly, not static JSON mining) would let a future round test whether they index a real table rather than being arbitrary per-move constants.

hitModifier's newly-confirmed nonzero values (2,6,18,20,25,30,34 across battle/support/item, all rare) and the hitProperties bit2 (0x4)/bit1-without-bit0 discoveries both indicate under-sampled bit/value space that a 4-character sample could not reveal; a disassembly trace of the code that reads hitModifier and hitProperties (not attempted in this data-only round) is now higher-value than before, since there are concrete nonzero real-world instances (bl_b_03, db_b_07, op_b_03, sk_b_02, tr_b_01 for hitModifier) to set a breakpoint/target on.

The support-file projectileId nonzero rate (23.03%) being ~10x the battle rate (2.30%) is the strongest lead in this round for the projectileId-marks-projectiles hypothesis; a targeted look at WHICH support characters carry nonzero projectileId (already listed per-file by this round's miner, not reproduced in full here for space) cross-referenced against docs/research/Character-Mapping.md's per-character support descriptions (pets/thrown items/helpers) would let a future pass test the 'support structs are structurally projectiles' hypothesis suggested by this round's SPECULATIVE finding without needing an emulator.
